MatchedObjectDescriptor.QualificationSummary: In addition to the Basic Requirements for this position, your resume must also demonstrate at least one year of specialized experience at or equivalent to the GS-12 grade level or pay band in the Federal service or equivalent experience in the private or public sector. Specialized experience must demonstrate the following: Experience displaying the mastery of skills in the concepts, principles and practices of nuclear engineering. Experience serving as a technical authority on projects relating to the overhaul or conversion of reactor plants for nuclear powered vessels. Experience, knowledge and skill sufficient to coordinate and review engineering project activities as a project engineer concerned with all phases of shipyard work on reactor plants including project planning functions relating to the refueling, alteration, repair, maintenance, and testing of nuclear reactor plants. Experience related to engineering fields such as mechanical and electrical. Additional qualification information can be found from the following Office of Personnel Management website: https://www.opm.gov/policy-data-oversight/classification-qualifications/general-schedule-qualification-standards/#url=List-by-Occupational-Series https://www.opm.gov/policy-data-oversight/classification-qualifications/general-schedule-qualification-standards/0800/files/all-professional-engineering-positions-0800.pdf Experience refers to paid and unpaid experience, including volunteer work done through National Service programs (e.g., professional, philanthropic, religious, spiritual, community, student, social). Volunteer work helps build critical competencies, knowledge, and skills and can provide valuable training and experience that translates directly to paid employment.

Details.JobSummary: You will serve as a NUCLEAR ENGINEER (Project Engineering Planning Manager) in the Assistant Nuclear Engineering and Planning Manager (Code 2301) of the Nuclear Engineering and Planning Department (Code 2300) at the Norfolk Naval Shipyard in Portsmouth, VA.
Details.AgencyMarketingStatement: The Navy and Marine Corps team offers innovative, exciting and meaningful work linking military and civilian talents to achieve our mission and safeguard our freedoms. Department of the Navy provides competitive salaries, comprehensive benefits, and extensive professional development and training. From pipefitters to accountants, scientists to engineers, doctors to nurses-the careers and opportunities to make a difference are endless. Civilian careers-where purpose and patriotism unite!
MajorDuties: You will coordinate across organizations lines withing the Nuclear Engineering Department, with other shipyard departments and various contractor representatives.
You will resolve conflicts concerning the work package development, overlapping functions, provide advice and ensure strict adherence to schedules.
You will identify requirements and provide directions for shipyard reactor plant work.
You will review all approved work completely and thoroughly.
You will assign cognizant technical codes, determine adequacy of software schedules for all major project assignments.
Details.Education: Applicants must meet the following positive education qualifications requirements of the Office of Personnel Management (OPM) Qualifications Standards Manual. Applicants must possess: Basic Requirements: A. Degree: Engineering. To be acceptable, the program must: (1) lead to a bachelor's degree in a school of engineering with at least one program accredited by ABET; or (2) include differential and integral calculus and courses (more advanced than first-year physics and chemistry) in five of the following seven areas of engineering science or physics: (a) statics, dynamics; (b) strength of materials (stress-strain relationships); (c) fluid mechanics, hydraulics; (d) thermodynamics; (e) electrical fields and circuits; (f) nature and properties of materials (relating particle and aggregate structure to properties); and (g) any other comparable area of fundamental engineering science or physics, such as optics, heat transfer, soil mechanics, or electronics. OR B. Combination of education and experience -- college-level education, training, and/or technical experience that furnished (1) a thorough knowledge of the physical and mathematical sciences underlying engineering, and (2) a good understanding, both theoretical and practical, of the engineering sciences and techniques and their applications to one of the branches of engineering. The adequacy of such background must be demonstrated by one of the following: 1. Professional registration or licensure -- Current registration as an Engineer Intern (EI), Engineer in Training (EIT)1, or licensure as a Professional Engineer (PE) by any State, the District of Columbia, Guam, or Puerto Rico. Absent other means of qualifying under this standard, those applicants who achieved such registration by means other than written test (e.g., State grandfather or eminence provisions) are eligible only for positions that are within or closely related to the specialty field of their registration. For example, an applicant who attains registration through a State Board's eminence provision as a manufacturing engineer typically would be rated eligible only for manufacturing engineering positions. 2. Written Test -- Evidence of having successfully passed the Fundamentals of Engineering (FE)2 examination or any other written test required for professional registration by an engineering licensure board in the various States, the District of Columbia, Guam, and Puerto Rico. 3. Specified academic courses -- Successful completion of at least 60 semester hours of courses in the physical, mathematical, and engineering sciences and that included the courses specified in the basic requirements under paragraph A. The courses must be fully acceptable toward meeting the requirements of an engineering program as described in paragraph A. 4. Related curriculum -- Successful completion of a curriculum leading to a bachelor's degree in an appropriate scientific field, e.g., engineering technology, physics, chemistry, architecture, computer science, mathematics, hydrology, or geology, may be accepted in lieu of a bachelor's degree in engineering, provided the applicant has had at least 1 year of professional engineering experience acquired under professional engineering supervision and guidance. Ordinarily there should be either an established plan of intensive training to develop professional engineering competence, or several years of prior professional engineering-type experience, e.g., in interdisciplinary positions. (The above examples of related curricula are not all-inclusive.)

MatchedObjectDescriptor.QualificationSummary: Your resume must demonstrate at least one year of specialized experience at or equivalent to the GS-12 grade level or pay band in the Federal service or equivalent experience in the private or public sector. Specialized experience must demonstrate the following: Experience technical concepts, principles and practices of project management sufficient to manage, coordinate, review and provide expert technical/engineering guidance and advice in detail for complex maintenance, repair, construction and overhaul of a variety of naval vessel classes of nuclear ships including one of a kind vessel or development systems. Experience serving as a technical expert performing the most complex and significant project management duties within the cognizance of the branch. Experience exercising creativity and experienced judgment in order to plan and prioritize the sequence and technical direction of work, extend traditional techniques or develop new ones to solve complex project management problems, modify and adapt existing processes and techniques to suit the specifics of work assignment. Experience preparing a schedule for technical working documents for repair and modernization, for nuclear systems on classes listed above. Experience understanding, adhering, ability to communicate technical authority policy and responsibilities throughout the NAVSEA chain-of-command (NNSY NEPD, Naval Reactors Representatives Office (NRRO), Reactor Plant Planning Yard (RPPY) NAVSEA). Experience providing technical knowledge and engineering experience related to a variety of nuclear overhaul types: Planning Incremental Availabilities (PIAs), Dry-Docking Planned Incremental Availabilities (DPIAs), Selected Restricted Availabilities (SRAs), Dry-Docking Selected Restricted Availabilities (DSRAs), Depot Modernization Periods (DMPs), Depot Phased Maintenance Availabilities (DPMAs), Extended Overhaul Availabilities (EOHs), off yard availabilities, etc. Additional qualification information can be found from the following Office of Personnel Management website: https://www.opm.gov/policy-data-oversight/classification-qualifications/general-schedule-qualification-standards/#url=List-by-Occupational-Series Experience refers to paid and unpaid experience, including volunteer work done through National Service programs (e.g., professional, philanthropic, religious, spiritual, community, student, social). Volunteer work helps build critical competencies, knowledge, and skills and can provide valuable training and experience that translates directly to paid employment.

Details.JobSummary: You will serve as a Engineering Technician ( Nuclear) in the Project Support Branch (Code 2301.2), Office of the Assistant Engineering and Planning Manager (Code 2301), and the Nuclear Engineering and Planning Department (NEPD) (Code 2300), of NORFOLK NAVAL SHIPYARD.
Details.AgencyMarketingStatement: The Navy and Marine Corps team offers innovative, exciting and meaningful work linking military and civilian talents to achieve our mission and safeguard our freedoms. From pipefitters to accountants, scientists to engineers, doctors to nurses-the careers and opportunities to make a difference are endless. Civilian careers-where purpose and patriotism unite!
MajorDuties: You will assure the proper preparation of software schedules for planning products (Job Summaries, Technical Work Documents, and Material Requirements).

You will manage assigned Project Planning Time Table (PPTTs) commitments assuring proper staffing, timely completion and budgetary control involving the overhaul or conversion of the reactor plants for nuclear powered submarines and surface ships.
You will develop and provide technical direction for the preparation and review of the ship?s overhaul schedules based on analysis of nuclear engineering work and other work to be performed
You will provide extensive coordination across the NEPD, other NNSY departments and other various contractor representatives

Details.JobSummary: You will serve as a SUPERVISORY NUCLEAR ENGINEER in the Radiological Emergency Planning Division (Code 105.6), Manager Radiological Controls Support Division (Code 105.1S), Radiological Control Office (Code 105) of NORFOLK NAVAL SHIPYARD.
Details.AgencyMarketingStatement: The Navy and Marine Corps team offers innovative, exciting and meaningful work linking military and civilian talents to achieve our mission and safeguard our freedoms. Department of the Navy provides competitive salaries, comprehensive benefits, and extensive professional development and training. From pipefitters to accountants, scientists to engineers, doctors to nurses-the careers and opportunities to make a difference are endless. Civilian careers-where purpose and patriotism unite!
MajorDuties: You will be responsible for the development of overall Shipyard emergency planning for potential radiological emergencies.
You will develop technical radiological statements for release to the news media during emergency conditions.
You will provide training where necessary for outside agencies and facilities.
You will plan and conduct major radiological emergency drills to evaluate Shipyard's level of readiness.
You will be assigned to carry out engineering evaluation, development, and application of new technology that impacts radiological emergency procedures and/or operations.
Details.Education: Applicants must meet the following basic education requirements of the Office of Personnel Management (OPM) Qualifications Standards Manual: Successful completion of a professional engineering degree. To be acceptable, the program must: (1) lead to a bachelor's degree (or higher) in a school of engineering with at least one program accredited by the Accreditation Board for Engineering and Technology (ABET); or (2) include differential and integral calculus and courses (more advanced than first-year physics and chemistry) in five of the following seven areas of engineering science or physics: (a) statics, dynamics; (b) strength of materials (stress-strain relationships); (c) fluid mechanics, hydraulics; (d) thermodynamics; (e) electrical fields and circuits; (f) nature and properties of materials (relating particle and aggregate structure to properties); and (g) any other comparable area of fundamental engineering science or physics, such as optics, heat transfer, soil mechanics, or electronics. Such education must demonstrate the knowledge, skills, and abilities necessary to do the work of the position. OR Current registration as an Engineer Intern (EI), Engineer in Training (EIT), or licensure as a Professional Engineer (PE) by any State, the District of Columbia, Guam, or Puerto Rico. Absent other means of qualifying under this standard, those applicants who achieved such registration by means other than written test (e.g., State grandfather or eminence provisions) are eligible only for positions that are within or closely related to the specialty field of their registration For more information about EI and EIT registration requirements, please visit the National Society of Professional Engineers website at: http://www.nspe.org OR Evidence of having successfully passed the Fundamentals of Engineering (FE) examination or any other written test required for professional registration by an engineering licensure board in the various States, the District of Columbia, Guam, and Puerto Rico The FE examination is not administered by the U. S. Office of Personnel Management. For more information, please visit: http://www.nspe.org/Licensure/HowtoGetLicensed/index.html. OR Successful completion of at least 60 semester hours of courses in the physical, mathematical, and engineering sciences and in engineering that included the courses specified in the basic requirements under paragraph A (above). The courses must be fully acceptable toward meeting the requirements of an engineering program as described in paragraph A (above) OR Successful completion of a curriculum leading to a bachelor's degree in an appropriate scientific field, e.g., engineering technology, physics, chemistry, architecture, computer science, mathematics, hydrology, or geology, may be accepted in lieu of a bachelor's degree in engineering, provided the applicant has had at least one year of professional engineering experience acquired under professional engineering supervision and guidance. Ordinarily, there should be either an established plan of intensive training to develop professional engineering competence, or several years of prior professional engineering-type experience, e.g., in interdisciplinary positions.

Details.JobSummary: You will serve as a ENGINEERING TECHNICIAN (MECHANICAL) in the FIRE FIGHTING/AUXILIARIES POLLUTION of SOUTHWEST REGIONAL MAINTENANCE CENTER.
Details.AgencyMarketingStatement: The Navy and Marine Corps team offers innovative, exciting and meaningful work linking military and civilian talents to achieve our mission and safeguard our freedoms. Department of the Navy provides competitive salaries, comprehensive benefits, and extensive professional development and training. From pipefitters to accountants, scientists to engineers, doctors to nurses-the careers and opportunities to make a difference are endless. Civilian careers-where purpose and patriotism unite!
MajorDuties: You will diagnose and correct shipboard equipment and systems relating to Fire Fighting / Damage Control Systems, Potable Water, Solid Waste, Sewage (CHT/VCHT), and Oil Pollution Abatement systems to resolve complex technical problems.

You will assess, troubleshoot, perform maintenance and training, and provide repair recommendations on shipboard Fire Fighting equipment/systems, associated piping, pumps, valves, and review shipboard Temporary Fire Protection Plans for accuracy.
You will assess, troubleshoot, perform maintenance and training, and provide repair recommendations on shipboard equipment/systems.

You will collaborate with the appropriate Technical Warrant Holders (TWH), Ship Design Managers (SDM) and In-Service Engineering Agents (ISEA) to ensure technical authority, risk management and engineering practices are properly implemented.

You will provide authoritative technical/engineering guidance to Waterfront Operations Project Managers and private shipyard engineering department personnel in resolution of repair/overhaul or test problems.
You will review drawings, technical manuals, specifications and product data sheets when a question arises to determine if a deviation or waiver can be allowed.

You will prepare comprehensive technical reports when required, formal correspondence, conduct out-briefs to customers and management to report findings and plan of action to resolve equipment/system problems.
You will perform special engineering analyses and studies on shipboard equipment and systems relating to Fire Fighting, Auxiliaries and Pollution Abatement.
You will provide on-site or distance technical assistance on urgent mission-degrading casualty reports (CASREPs) or similar problems.
You will represent the Board of Inspections and Surveys (INSURV) in the inspection and functional checkout/ demonstration of major shipboard systems on new construction ships or major conversions.

MatchedObjectDescriptor.QualificationSummary: TO QUALIFY FOR THE GS -12: Your resume must demonstrate at least one year of specialized experience at or equivalent to the GS-11 grade level or pay band in the Federal service or equivalent experience in the private or public sector. Specialized experience must demonstrate the following:1) Managing the execution of work processes and equipment inventory in support of the Vertical Transportation Equipment (VTE) inspection and certification program; 2) Applying technical engineering expertise of related engineering fields to ensure areas of overlapping disciplines (mechanical, electrical, fire protection, hydraulics, etc.) receive proper design considerations and that all project requirements are met; 3) Performing inspections and certifications of existing, altered or new VTE to determine if systems / parts / devices conform to NFPA, NEC, ASME, ANSI or other applicable safety regulations and building codes: 4) Communicating effectively both orally and in writing at a professional level when interfacing with customers and organizational stakeholders; and 5) Utilizing a computer and application software (i.e. MS Office Suite, MS Project, Maximo, SLDCADA, etc.) to perform communication / productivity tasks and activities. NOTE: This information must be supported in your resume for you to receive further consideration for this position. For the GS-12 Position: The incumbent will be required to obtain a Naval Facilities Engineering Command Vertical Transportation Equipment (NAVFAC VTE) License/Certification within the first 12 months of employment. The incumbent must possess an American Society of Mechanical Engineers (ASME) Qualified Elevator Inspector (QEI) Certification per Public Works (PW) BMS B-15.12 - Vertical Transportation Equipment Program at the time of entry. TO QUALIFY FOR THE GS -11: Outside applicants claiming VEOA, E.O. 13473, SCHEDULE A, (i.e. those without current or prior Federal competitive or excepted service) must meet specialized experience requirements at the GS-10 grade level or equivalent in the public or private sector. The applicant resume must demonstrate at least one year of specialized experience at or equivalent to the GS-10 grade level or pay band in the Federal service or equivalent experience in the private or public sector. Specialized experience must demonstrate the following: 1) Applying basic knowledge of building codes, industry standards, safety regulations, OSHA standards, environmental regulations and facilities maintenance procedures; 2) Testing instruments used during the VTE inspection / certification process to include thickness gages, rope calipers, sheave groove gages, stop watches, tachometers, multi meters, meggers, door test scale gages, light meters and all related safety equipment; 3) Reading and interpreting blueprints, specifications, sketches, technical directives, inspection orders, and work requests; 4) Communicating effectively both orally and in writing at a professional level when interfacing with customers and organizational stakeholders; 5) Utilizing a computer and application software (i.e. MS Office Suite, MS Project, Maximo, SLDCADA, etc.) to perform communication / productivity tasks and activities; and 6) Performing evaluation of existing equipment for replacement or repair. Applicants who are current Federal competitive or excepted service employees must meet specialized experience requirement at the GS-09 grade level or equivalent pay band. The applicant resume must demonstrate at least one year of specialized experience at or equivalent to the GS-09 grade level or pay band in the Federal service or equivalent experience in the private or public sector. Specialized experience must demonstrate the following: 1) Applying basic knowledge of building codes, industry standards, safety regulations, OSHA standards, environmental regulations and facilities maintenance procedures; 2) Testing instruments used during the VTE inspection / certification process to include thickness gages, rope calipers, sheave groove gages, stop watches, tachometers, multi meters, meggers, door test scale gages, light meters and all related safety equipment; 3) Reading and interpreting blueprints, specifications, sketches, technical directives, inspection orders, and work requests; 4) Communicating effectively both orally and in writing at a professional level when interfacing with customers and organizational stakeholders; 5) Utilizing a computer and application software (i.e. MS Office Suite, MS Project, Maximo, SLDCADA, etc.) to perform communication / productivity tasks and activities. For the GS-11 Position: The incumbent will be required to obtain a Naval Facilities Engineering Command Vertical Transportation Equipment (NAVFAC VTE) License/Certification within the first 12 months of employment. The incumbent will be required to obtain an American Society of Mechanical Engineers (ASME) Qualified Elevator Inspector (QEI) Certification per Public Works (PW) BMS B-15.12 - Vertical Transportation Equipment Program within in 24 months after obtaining the Naval Facilities Engineering Command Vertical Transportation Equipment (NAVFAC VTE) License/Certification. The incumbent cannot be promoted to the GS-12 level without a QEI certification. Additional qualification information can be found from the following Office of Personnel Management website: https://www.opm.gov/policy-data-oversight/classification-qualifications/general-schedule-qualification-standards/#url=List-by-Occupational-Series Experience refers to paid and unpaid experience, including volunteer work done through National Service programs (e.g., professional, philanthropic, religious, spiritual, community, student, social). Volunteer work helps build critical competencies, knowledge, and skills and can provide valuable training and experience that translates directly to paid employment.

MatchedObjectDescriptor.QualificationSummary: FOR THE GS-12: Your resume must demonstrate at least one year of specialized experience at or equivalent to the GS-11 grade level or pay band in the Federal service or equivalent experience in the private or public sector as a professional engineer or naval architect developing detailed specifications for ship overhaul/modernization, and providing technical direction for the execution of ship design projects, resolving technical issues or to develop engineered solutions to problems related to ship systems or equipment. FOR THE GS-11: Education may be substituted for specialized experience as follows: Successful completion of a Ph.D. or equivalent doctoral degree -OR- Successful completion of three full years of progressively higher level graduate education leading to a Ph.D. or equivalent degree -OR- A combination of experience and education as described above that equates to one year of experience Additional qualification information can be found from the following Office of Personnel Management website: https://www.opm.gov/policy-data-oversight/classification-qualifications/general-schedule-qualification-standards/#url=List-by-Occupational-Series AND https://www.opm.gov/policy-data-oversight/classification-qualifications/general-schedule-qualification-standards/0800/files/all-professional-engineering-positions-0800.pdf Experience refers to paid and unpaid experience, including volunteer work done through National Service programs (e.g., professional, philanthropic, religious, spiritual, community, student, social). Details.JobSummary: You will serve as a NAVAL ARCHITECT in the ENGINEERING DEPARTMENT, NAVAL ARCHITECTURE, STRUCTURES, CORROSION CONTROL, & PASSIVE MEASURE COUNTER SYSTEM DIVISION of SOUTHWEST REGIONAL MAINTENANCE CENTER.
Details.AgencyMarketingStatement: The Navy and Marine Corps team offers innovative, exciting and meaningful work linking military and civilian talents to achieve our mission and safeguard our freedoms. Department of the Navy provides competitive salaries, comprehensive benefits, and extensive professional development and training. From pipefitters to accountants, scientists to engineers, doctors to nurses-the careers and opportunities to make a difference are endless. Civilian careers-where purpose and patriotism unite! Headquartered at Pearl Harbor on the island of Oahu in Hawaii, this four-star command is the world's largest fleet command. Encompassing 100 million square miles, our 200 ships/submarines, nearly 1,200 aircraft, and more than 130,000 uniformed and civilian Sailors serve on nearly half of the Earth's surface -- from Antarctica to the Arctic Circle, and from the U.S. West Coast to the Indian Ocean. Join the USPACFLT team to achieve more and to help protect and defend the maritime interests of the U.S. in the Indo-Pacific, providing combat-ready forces and operating forward, ready to fight tonight. We want talent and enthusiasm aboard the USPACFLT team. We want the best! For further information, please visit https://www.cpf.navy.mil/.
MajorDuties: You will provide engineering services for ship modifications, testing, work control, temporary services, and manufacturing products, in relation to Naval Architecture and ship structure.
You will make investigations aboard ship to obtain information for development of or determine adaptability of working plans.
You will provide Technical Assistance to our surface fleet in the form of structural inspections/assessments and technical adjudication.
You will ensure timely, technically accurate execution of complex design projects, documents or drawing development or planning projects.
You will perform engineering studies to determine systems requirements, modifications, repairs or specifications in relation to Naval Architecture and ship structure.
You will identify, develop and implement process improvement initiatives to support improvement initiatives.

You will conduct independent engineering studies, investigations, research and analysis for the solution of unusual or unprecedented engineering problems or in support of short- and long-term engineering projects.
You will prepare and direct the development of engineering reports and correspondences relating to specific work projects.
You will review contractor work specifications and other contractual documents for technical adequacy and provides government oversight ensuring the naval requirements in tasking documents are met.
Details.Education: Applicants must meet the following basic education requirements of the Office of Personnel Management (OPM) Qualifications Standards Manual: Successful completion of a professional engineering degree. To be acceptable, the program must: (1) lead to a bachelor's degree (or higher) in a school of engineering with at least one program accredited by the Accreditation Board for Engineering and Technology (ABET); or (2) include differential and integral calculus and courses (more advanced than first-year physics and chemistry) in five of the following seven areas of engineering science or physics: (a) statics, dynamics; (b) strength of materials (stress-strain relationships); (c) fluid mechanics, hydraulics; (d) thermodynamics; (e) electrical fields and circuits; (f) nature and properties of materials (relating particle and aggregate structure to properties); and (g) any other comparable area of fundamental engineering science or physics, such as optics, heat transfer, soil mechanics, or electronics. Such education must demonstrate the knowledge, skills, and abilities necessary to do the work of the position. OR Current registration as an Engineer Intern (EI), Engineer in Training (EIT), or licensure as a Professional Engineer (PE) by any State, the District of Columbia, Guam, or Puerto Rico. Absent other means of qualifying under this standard, those applicants who achieved such registration by means other than written test (e.g., State grandfather or eminence provisions) are eligible only for positions that are within or closely related to the specialty field of their registration For more information about EI and EIT registration requirements, please visit the National Society of Professional Engineers website at: http://www.nspe.org OR Evidence of having successfully passed the Fundamentals of Engineering (FE) examination or any other written test required for professional registration by an engineering licensure board in the various States, the District of Columbia, Guam, and Puerto Rico The FE examination is not administered by the U. S. Office of Personnel Management. For more information, please visit: http://www.nspe.org/Licensure/HowtoGetLicensed/index.html. OR Successful completion of at least 60 semester hours of courses in the physical, mathematical, and engineering sciences and in engineering that included the courses specified in the basic requirements under paragraph A (above). The courses must be fully acceptable toward meeting the requirements of an engineering program as described in paragraph A (above) OR Successful completion of a curriculum leading to a bachelor's degree in an appropriate scientific field, e.g., engineering technology, physics, chemistry, architecture, computer science, mathematics, hydrology, or geology, may be accepted in lieu of a bachelor's degree in engineering, provided the applicant has had at least one year of professional engineering experience acquired under professional engineering supervision and guidance. Ordinarily, there should be either an established plan of intensive training to develop professional engineering competence, or several years of prior professional engineering-type experience, e.g., in interdisciplinary positions.

Details.JobSummary: You will serve as a LEAD ENGINEERING TECHNICIAN (ELECTRICAL) in the Electrical Distribution and Power Generation Branch (Code 262) of the Main Propulsion and Electrical Division (Code 260) of the Engineering Department (Code 200) of SOUTHWEST REGIONAL MAINTENANCE CENTER, San Diego, California.

Details.AgencyMarketingStatement: The Navy and Marine Corps team offers innovative, exciting and meaningful work linking military and civilian talents to achieve our mission and safeguard our freedoms. Department of the Navy provides competitive salaries, comprehensive benefits, and extensive professional development and training. From pipefitters to accountants, scientists to engineers, doctors to nurses-the careers and opportunities to make a difference are endless. Headquartered at Pearl Harbor on the island of Oahu in Hawaii, this four-star command is the world's largest fleet command. Encompassing 100 million square miles, our 200 ships/submarines, nearly 1,200 aircraft, and more than 130,000 uniformed and civilian Sailors serve on nearly half of the Earth's surface -- from Antarctica to the Arctic Circle, and from the U.S. West Coast to the Indian Ocean. Join the USPACFLT team to achieve more and to help protect and defend the maritime interests of the U.S. in the Indo-Pacific, providing combat-ready forces and operating forward, ready to fight tonight. We want talent and enthusiasm aboard the USPACFLT team. We want the best! For further information, please visit https://www.cpf.navy.mil/. Civilian careers-where purpose and patriotism unite!
MajorDuties: You will serve as lead technical expert on Electrical Distribution and Power Generation systems, providing expert repair guidance, including thorough risk analysis and repair options,

You will provide expertise for systems onboard naval ships for High and Low Voltage, and DC Distribution Systems, Switchboards, Circuit Breakers, ABT Switches, Power Generation, Electrical Propulsion, and Frequency Conversion systems,

You will serve as a lead technical representative for shipboard, intermediate, and depot-level technical assistance on problems determined to be beyond capability of ships force, Intermediate Maintenance Activity, and ship repair facility level,

You will serve as Team Leader of Technical Teams with responsibility for functional checks, test and inspection, and material condition assessment of major electrical distribution and power generation systems,
You will provide oversight to ships force, intermediate level personnel and contractors performing repairs; prioritize work; resolve conflicts, and brief senior Command Leadership,
You will coordinate with codes throughout SWRMC Engineering, and liaison with NAVSEA, Naval Station Warfare Center Philadelphia, Type Commander, Naval Shipyards and other technical groups.

Details.JobSummary: You will serve as a GENERAL ENGINEER in the Explosive Ordnance Engineering Group, (SEA 05E) of NAVSEA HQ FIELD SUPPORT. You will serve as a subject matter expert for Anti-Terrorism/Force Protection (AT/FP) and Small Arms efforts within NAVSEA.
Details.AgencyMarketingStatement: The Navy and Marine Corps team offers innovative, exciting and meaningful work linking military and civilian talents to achieve our mission and safeguard our freedoms. Department of the Navy provides competitive salaries, comprehensive benefits, and extensive professional development and training. From pipefitters to accountants, scientists to engineers, doctors to nurses-the careers and opportunities to make a difference are endless. Civilian careers-where purpose and patriotism unite!
MajorDuties: You will support the Technical Warrant Holders (TWH's) for AT/FP and Small Arms engineering efforts.
You will provide technical oversight of requirements, specifications, system and analysis, design criteria, design products and waivers.
You will prepare technical adjudication reports on the application of AT/FP and Small Arms systems and trade studies.
You will capture, coordinate, and documents TWH assessments, risks, and issues related to systems technology and products.
You will demonstrate experience with Anti-Terrorism/Force Protection and Small Arms as they apply to defense system applications.

You will provide authoritative technical, scientific, and/or professional advice to senior level leadership concerning unusual or critical problems that often affect the work of internal and external stakeholders.
You will serve as a recognized expert and consultant to ensure reliability and accuracy in the identification, development and implementation of recommended solutions to highly complex problems.
Details.Education: Applicants must meet the following basic education requirements of the Office of Personnel Management (OPM) Qualifications Standards Manual: Successful completion of a professional engineering degree. To be acceptable, the program must: (1) lead to a bachelor's degree (or higher) in a school of engineering with at least one program accredited by the Accreditation Board for Engineering and Technology (ABET); or (2) include differential and integral calculus and courses (more advanced than first-year physics and chemistry) in five of the following seven areas of engineering science or physics: (a) statics, dynamics; (b) strength of materials (stress-strain relationships); (c) fluid mechanics, hydraulics; (d) thermodynamics; (e) electrical fields and circuits; (f) nature and properties of materials (relating particle and aggregate structure to properties); and (g) any other comparable area of fundamental engineering science or physics, such as optics, heat transfer, soil mechanics, or electronics. Such education must demonstrate the knowledge, skills, and abilities necessary to do the work of the position. OR Current registration as an Engineer Intern (EI), Engineer in Training (EIT), or licensure as a Professional Engineer (PE) by any State, the District of Columbia, Guam, or Puerto Rico. Absent other means of qualifying under this standard, those applicants who achieved such registration by means other than written test (e.g., State grandfather or eminence provisions) are eligible only for positions that are within or closely related to the specialty field of their registration For more information about EI and EIT registration requirements, please visit the National Society of Professional Engineers website at: http://www.nspe.org OR Evidence of having successfully passed the Fundamentals of Engineering (FE) examination or any other written test required for professional registration by an engineering licensure board in the various States, the District of Columbia, Guam, and Puerto Rico The FE examination is not administered by the U. S. Office of Personnel Management. For more information, please visit: http://www.nspe.org/Licensure/HowtoGetLicensed/index.html. OR Successful completion of at least 60 semester hours of courses in the physical, mathematical, and engineering sciences and in engineering that included the courses specified in the basic requirements under paragraph A (above). The courses must be fully acceptable toward meeting the requirements of an engineering program as described in paragraph A (above) OR Successful completion of a curriculum leading to a bachelor's degree in an appropriate scientific field, e.g., engineering technology, physics, chemistry, architecture, computer science, mathematics, hydrology, or geology, may be accepted in lieu of a bachelor's degree in engineering, provided the applicant has had at least one year of professional engineering experience acquired under professional engineering supervision and guidance. Ordinarily, there should be either an established plan of intensive training to develop professional engineering competence, or several years of prior professional engineering-type experience, e.g., in interdisciplinary positions.

Details.JobSummary: You will serve as a PROGRAM MANAGER in the STRUCTURES & COMPOSITES DIVISION within the PLATFORM INTEGRITY DEPT of CARDEROCK DIV NS. This position is part of the Warfare Centers Personnel Demonstration Project. The ND-4 pay band encompasses positions equivalent to the GS-12 and GS-13.
Details.AgencyMarketingStatement: The Navy and Marine Corps team offers innovative, exciting and meaningful work linking military and civilian talents to achieve our mission and safeguard our freedoms. Department of the Navy provides competitive salaries, comprehensive benefits, and extensive professional development and training. From pipefitters to accountants, scientists to engineers, doctors to nurses-the careers and opportunities to make a difference are endless. Civilian careers-where purpose and patriotism unite!
MajorDuties: You will manage a portfolio of research and development tasks for submarine and undersea structures programs.
You will develop statements of work, budgets, and schedules that support multi-year programs.
You will work with NAVSEA technical community and acquisition program offices on technical programs with an emphasis on Navy structures.
You will brief program status to sponsors, technical leaders and organizational leaders.
You will identify resource needs to support research and development efforts, and work with management to address the needs.
Details.Education: Applicants must meet the following basic education requirements of the Office of Personnel Management (OPM) Qualifications Standards Manual: Successful completion of a professional engineering degree. To be acceptable, the program must: (1) lead to a bachelor's degree (or higher) in a school of engineering with at least one program accredited by the Accreditation Board for Engineering and Technology (ABET); or (2) include differential and integral calculus and courses (more advanced than first-year physics and chemistry) in five of the following seven areas of engineering science or physics: (a) statics, dynamics; (b) strength of materials (stress-strain relationships); (c) fluid mechanics, hydraulics; (d) thermodynamics; (e) electrical fields and circuits; (f) nature and properties of materials (relating particle and aggregate structure to properties); and (g) any other comparable area of fundamental engineering science or physics, such as optics, heat transfer, soil mechanics, or electronics. Such education must demonstrate the knowledge, skills, and abilities necessary to do the work of the position. OR Current registration as an Engineer Intern (EI), Engineer in Training (EIT), or licensure as a Professional Engineer (PE) by any State, the District of Columbia, Guam, or Puerto Rico. Absent other means of qualifying under this standard, those applicants who achieved such registration by means other than written test (e.g., State grandfather or eminence provisions) are eligible only for positions that are within or closely related to the specialty field of their registration For more information about EI and EIT registration requirements, please visit the National Society of Professional Engineers website at: http://www.nspe.org OR Evidence of having successfully passed the Fundamentals of Engineering (FE) examination or any other written test required for professional registration by an engineering licensure board in the various States, the District of Columbia, Guam, and Puerto Rico The FE examination is not administered by the U. S. Office of Personnel Management. For more information, please visit: http://www.nspe.org/Licensure/HowtoGetLicensed/index.html. OR Successful completion of at least 60 semester hours of courses in the physical, mathematical, and engineering sciences and in engineering that included the courses specified in the basic requirements under paragraph A (above). The courses must be fully acceptable toward meeting the requirements of an engineering program as described in paragraph A (above) OR Successful completion of a curriculum leading to a bachelor's degree in an appropriate scientific field, e.g., engineering technology, physics, chemistry, architecture, computer science, mathematics, hydrology, or geology, may be accepted in lieu of a bachelor's degree in engineering, provided the applicant has had at least one year of professional engineering experience acquired under professional engineering supervision and guidance. Ordinarily, there should be either an established plan of intensive training to develop professional engineering competence, or several years of prior professional engineering-type experience, e.g., in interdisciplinary positions.

You will develop standards, criteria, policies and overall long-range plans for the OSEMD.
You will coordinate, review, and evaluate the work performed by engineers, technicians, supply analysts, project managers, vendors, contract personnel, and contract facilities personnel.

You will make plans for new equipment and improved facilities.
You will provide senior level engineering support to the OSEMD, NMCLANT Command, and customer commands.
You will conduct system analyses of test, measurement, and maintenance processes for wide variety of complex systems and subsystems.
You will provide engineering and management advice on especially difficult and novel problems to Command, Fleet, Headquarters, and other customers.

You will be asked to identify which category or categories you meet, and to provide documents which prove you meet the category or categories you selected. See Proof of Eligibility for an extensive list of document requirements for all employment authorities. Interagency Career Transition Assistance PlanPriority Placement Program, DoD Military Spouse Preference (MSP) Eligible In order to qualify, you must meet the education and experience requirements described below. Experience refers to paid and unpaid experience, including volunteer work done through National Service programs (e.g., Peace Corps, AmeriCorps) and other organizations (e.g., professional; philanthropic; religious; spiritual; community; student; social). You will receive credit for all qualifying experience, including volunteer experience. Your resume must clearly describe your relevant experience; if qualifying based on education, your transcripts will be required as part of your application. Additional information about transcripts is in this document. Requirements for Civil Engineer (Hydraulics), GS-13: Basic Requirement for Civil Engineer (Hydraulics): A. Degree: Bachelor's degree (or higher degree) in engineering. To be acceptable, the program must: (1) lead to a bachelor's degree (or higher degree) in a school of engineering with at least one program accredited by the Accreditation Board for Engineering and Technology (ABET); OR (2) include differential and integral calculus and courses (more advanced than first-year physics and chemistry) in five of the following seven areas of engineering science or physics: (a) statics, dynamics; (b) strength of materials (stress-strain relationships); (c) fluid mechanics, hydraulics; (d) thermodynamics; (e) electrical fields and circuits; (f) nature and properties of materials (relating particle and aggregate structure to properties); and (g) any other comparable area of fundamental engineering science or physics, such as optics, heat transfer, soil mechanics, or electronics. OR B. Combination of Education and Experience: College-level education, training, and/or technical experience that furnished (1) a thorough knowledge of the physical and mathematical sciences underlying engineering, and (2) a good understanding, both theoretical and practical, of the engineering sciences and techniques and their applications to one of the branches of engineering. The adequacy of such background must be demonstrated by one of the following: 1. Professional registration or licensure - Current registration as an Engineer Intern (EI), Engineer in Training (EIT), or licensure as a Professional Engineer (PE) by any State, the District of Columbia, Guam, or Puerto Rico. Absent other means of qualifying under this standard, those applicants who achieved such registration by means other than written test (e.g., State grandfather or eminence provisions) are eligible only for positions that are within or closely related to the specialty field of their registration. For example, an applicant who attains registration through a State Board's eminence provision as a manufacturing engineer typically would be rated eligible only for manufacturing engineering positions. 2. Written Test - Evidence of having successfully passed the Fundamentals of Engineering (FE) examination, or any other written test required for professional registration, by an engineering licensure board in the various States, the District of Columbia, Guam, or Puerto Rico. 3. Specified academic courses - Successful completion of at least 60 semester hours of courses in the physical, mathematical, and engineering sciences and that included the courses specified in A above. The courses must be fully acceptable toward meeting the requirements of an engineering program. 4. Related curriculum - Successful completion of a curriculum leading to a bachelor's degree in an appropriate scientific field, e.g., engineering technology, physics, chemistry, architecture, computer science, mathematics, hydrology, or geology, may be accepted in lieu of a degree in engineering, provided the applicant has had at least 1 year of professional engineering experience acquired under professional engineering supervision and guidance. Ordinarily there should be either an established plan of intensive training to develop professional engineering competence, or several years of prior professional engineering-type experience, e.g., in interdisciplinary positions. In addition to meeting the basic requirement above, to qualify for this position you must also meet the qualification requirements listed below: Specialized Experience: One year of specialized experience which includes 1) conducting studies on the littoral cell characteristics; 2) developing modeling techniques to evaluate coastal processes; 3) determining optimum means for shoreline protection, AND; 4) conducting dredging and dredged material management analysis. AND Selective Placement Factor: This position requires the possession of an active Professional Engineering (PE) License issued by any State in the United States, the District of Columbia, Guam, or Puerto Rico. You will be evaluated on the basis of your level of competency in the following areas: Time in Grade Requirement: Applicants who have held a General Schedule (GS) position within the last 52 weeks must have 52 weeks of Federal service at the next lower grade or equivalent (GS-12).

Details.JobSummary: About the Position: As the District's expert in Coastal Engineering is technically responsible for carrying out the District's responsibilities for coastal engineering designs and development of detailed plans and specifications including special and unique monitoring programs for projects along coastal areas and inlets for the purposes of wetland restoration, navigation improvements, shoreline protection and beach erosion control.
Details.SubAgencyName: South Pacific Division, San Francisco District, Water Resources Section
Details.AgencyMarketingStatement: Looking for a great place to work? The U.S. Army Corps of Engineers is one of the best! In 2019, USACE ranked number three of government large-agency subcomponents! As rated by their employees, USACE supervisors strongly support employee development and opportunities to demonstrate leadership skills, while also maintaining an optimal work/life balance. The Corps offers a team-inspiring and collaborative work environment; providing challenging and rewarding careers across a variety of disciplines. Civilian employees serve a vital role in supporting the Army mission. They provide the skills that are not readily available in the military, but crucial to support military operations. The Army integrates the talents and skills of its military and civilian members to form a Total Army.
MajorDuties: Coordinates and consults with other District offices on the gathering and preparation of data for development of hydrodynamic and sediment transport models.
Provides expert recommendations for the conduct of special wind, wave, erosion and accretion studies.
Undertakes the design of navigation channels, sediment traps, floodwalls, levees, tidegates, backfills, jetties, breakwaters and groins and seawalls.
Develops procedures and standards to be used by others for wetland restoration, navigation improvements, shoreline protection and beach erosion control.
Directs section and unit engineers engaged in developing designs for projects along coastal areas, inlets and estuarine environments.
Plans and schedules work, directs employees, establishes priorities and periodically evaluates program activities to ascertain if program objectives are being met.
Establishes methods and procedures for effective accomplishment of work and reviews and approves completed work.

MatchedObjectDescriptor.QualificationSummary: Who May Apply: US Citizens In order to qualify, you must meet the education and experience requirements described below. Experience refers to paid and unpaid experience, including volunteer work done through National Service programs (e.g., Peace Corps, AmeriCorps) and other organizations (e.g., professional; philanthropic; religious; spiritual; community; student; social). You will receive credit for all qualifying experience, including volunteer experience. Your resume must clearly describe your relevant experience; if qualifying based on education, your transcripts will be required as part of your application. Additional information about transcripts is in this document. Basic Requirement for Engineering Positions: A. Degree: Bachelor's degree (or higher degree) in engineering. To be acceptable, the program must: (1) lead to a bachelor's degree (or higher degree) in a school of engineering with at least one program accredited by the Accreditation Board for Engineering and Technology (ABET); OR(2) include differential and integral calculus and courses (more advanced than first-year physics and chemistry) in five of the following seven areas of engineering science or physics: (a) statics, dynamics; (b) strength of materials (stress-strain relationships); (c) fluid mechanics, hydraulics;(d) thermodynamics; (e) electrical fields and circuits; (f) nature and properties of materials (relating particle and aggregate structure to properties); and (g) any other comparable area of fundamental engineering science or physics, such as optics, heat transfer, soil mechanics, or electronics. OR B. Combination of Education and Experience: College-level education, training, and/or technical experience that furnished (1) a thorough knowledge of the physical and mathematical sciences underlying engineering, and (2) a good understanding, both theoretical and practical, of the engineering sciences and techniques and their applications to one of the branches of engineering. The adequacy of such background must be demonstrated by one of the following: 1. Professional registration or licensure - Current registration as an Engineer Intern (EI), Engineer in Training (EIT), or licensure as a Professional Engineer (PE) by any State, the District of Columbia, Guam, or Puerto Rico. Absent other means of qualifying under this standard, those applicants who achieved such registration by means other than written test (e.g., State grandfather or eminence provisions) are eligible only for positions that are within or closely related to the specialty field of their registration. For example, an applicant who attains registration through a State Board's eminence provision as a manufacturing engineer typically would be rated eligible only for manufacturing engineering positions. 2.Written Test - Evidence of having successfully passed the Fundamentals of Engineering (FE) examination, or any other written test required for professional registration, by an engineering licensure board in the various States, the District of Columbia, Guam, or Puerto Rico. 3. Specified academic courses - Successful completion of at least 60 semester hours of courses in the physical, mathematical, and engineering sciences and that included the courses specified in A above. The courses must be fully acceptable toward meeting the requirements of an engineering program. 4. Related curriculum - Successful completion of a curriculum leading to a bachelor's degree in an appropriate scientific field, e.g., engineering technology, physics, chemistry, architecture, computer science, mathematics, hydrology, or geology, may be accepted in lieu of a degree in engineering, provided the applicant has had at least 1 year of professional engineering experience acquired under professional engineering supervision and guidance. Ordinarily there should be either an established plan of intensive training to develop professional engineering competence, or several years of prior professional engineering-type experience, e.g., in interdisciplinary positions. In addition to meeting the basic requirement above, to qualify for this position you must also meet the qualification requirements listed below: Specialized Experience for the GS 13 Position: One year of specialized experience in the Federal service which includes: 1) supervising or leading a team of interdisciplinary engineers and technicians; AND 2) working with contractors regarding project changes; AND 3) overseeing the preparation of design reports and solicitation packages for flood control projects. This definition of specialized experience is typical of work performed at the next lower grade/level position in the federal service (GS-12). Qualification requirement: Qualifications must be met by the closing date of this announcement. Some federal jobs allow you to substitute your education for the required experience in order to qualify. For this job, you must meet the qualification requirement using experience alone--no substitution of education for experience is permitted.

MatchedObjectDescriptor.QualificationSummary: Who May Apply: US Citizens In order to qualify, you must meet the education and/or experience requirements described below. Experience refers to paid and unpaid experience, including volunteer work done through National Service programs (e.g., Peace Corps, AmeriCorps) and other organizations (e.g., professional; philanthropic; religious; spiritual; community; student; social). You will receive credit for all qualifying experience, including volunteer experience. Your resume must clearly describe your relevant experience; if qualifying based on education, your transcripts will be required as part of your application. Additional information about transcripts is in this document. Basic Requirement for Biologist: A. Degree: Bachelor's degree (or higher degree) in biological sciences, agriculture, natural resource management, chemistry, or related disciplines appropriate to the position. OR B. Combination of Education and Experience: Courses equivalent to a major, as shown in A above, plus appropriate experience or additional education. Basic Requirement for Environmental Engineer: A. Degree: Bachelor's degree (or higher degree) in engineering. To be acceptable, the program must: (1) lead to a bachelor's degree (or higher degree) in a school of engineering with at least one program accredited by the Accreditation Board for Engineering and Technology (ABET); OR (2) include differential and integral calculus and courses (more advanced than first-year physics and chemistry) in five of the following seven areas of engineering science or physics: (a) statics, dynamics; (b) strength of materials (stress-strain relationships); (c) fluid mechanics, hydraulics; (d) thermodynamics; (e) electrical fields and circuits; (f) nature and properties of materials (relating particle and aggregate structure to properties); and (g) any other comparable area of fundamental engineering science or physics, such as optics, heat transfer, soil mechanics, or electronics. OR B. Combination of Education and Experience: College-level education, training, and/or technical experience that furnished (1) a thorough knowledge of the physical and mathematical sciences underlying engineering, and (2) a good understanding, both theoretical and practical, of the engineering sciences and techniques and their applications to one of the branches of engineering. The adequacy of such background must be demonstrated by one of the following:1. Professional registration or licensure - Current registration as an Engineer Intern (EI), Engineer in Training (EIT), or licensure as a Professional Engineer (PE) by any State, the District of Columbia, Guam, or Puerto Rico. Absent other means of qualifying under this standard, those applicants who achieved such registration by means other than written test (e.g., State grandfather or eminence provisions) are eligible only for positions that are within or closely related to the specialty field of their registration. For example, an applicant who attains registration through a State Board's eminence provision as a manufacturing engineer typically would be rated eligible only for manufacturing engineering positions.2. Written Test - Evidence of having successfully passed the Fundamentals of Engineering (FE) examination, or any other written test required for professional registration, by an engineering licensure board in the various States, the District of Columbia, Guam, or Puerto Rico.3. Specified academic courses - Successful completion of at least 60 semester hours of courses in the physical, mathematical, and engineering sciences and that included the courses specified in A above. The courses must be fully acceptable toward meeting the requirements of an engineering program.4. Related curriculum - Successful completion of a curriculum leading to a bachelor's degree in an appropriate scientific field, e.g., engineering technology, physics, chemistry, architecture, computer science, mathematics, hydrology, or geology, may be accepted in lieu of a degree in engineering, provided the applicant has had at least 1 year of professional engineering experience acquired under professional engineering supervision and guidance. Ordinarily there should be either an established plan of intensive training to develop professional engineering competence, or several years of prior professional engineering-type experience, e.g., in interdisciplinary positions. Basic Requirement for Physical Scientist: A. Degree: Bachelor's degree (or higher degree) in physical science, engineering, or mathematics that included 24 semester hours in physical science and/or related engineering science such as mechanics, dynamics, properties of materials, and electronics. OR B. Combination of Education and Experience: Courses equivalent to one of the majors, as shown in A above, that included at least 24 semester hours in physical science and/or related engineering science, plus appropriate experience or additional education. Basic Requirement for Geologist: A. Degree: Bachelor's degree (or higher degree) in geology, plus 20 additional semester hours in any combination of mathematics, physics, chemistry, biological science, structural, chemical, civil, mining or petroleum engineering, computer science, planetary geology, comparative planetology, geophysics, meteorology, hydrology, oceanography, physical geography, marine geology, and cartography. OR B. Combination of Education and Experience: Course work as shown in A above, plus appropriate experience or additional education. (Note: Acceptable experience may have been gained through geological field or laboratory work that provided a means of obtaining professional knowledge of the theory and application of the principles of geology and closely related sciences, e.g., geophysics, geochemistry, or hydrology. Such work generally must have involved making close observations, taking samples, handling various types of instruments and equipment, assembling geologic data from source materials, and analyzing and reporting findings orally and in writing. In some situations, professional scientific experience in other fields may be accepted in part as professional geological experience. Such experience must have been preceded by appropriate education in geology or by professional geological experience, and must have contributed directly and significantly to the applicant's professional geological competence. To receive credit for geological experience obtained in positions that are not full-time professional geological positions, the applicant is responsible for indicating clearly the actual time or percentage of time devoted to geologic duties within such positions, and for giving adequate descriptions of the geologic functions.) Basic Requirement for Oceanographer: A. Degree: Bachelor's degree (or higher degree) with a major study of at least 24 semester hours in oceanography or a related discipline such as physics, meteorology, geophysics, mathematics, chemistry, engineering, geology, or biology, plus 20 additional semester hours in any combination of oceanography, physics, geophysics, chemistry, mathematics, meteorology, computer science, and engineering sciences. Applicants who qualify on the basis of major study in biology or geology must have had at least 6 semester hours in the major directly concerned with marine science or 6 semester hours in oceanography; applicants who qualify on the basis of other physical sciences or engineering must have had differential and integral calculus and at least 6 semester hours in physics. OR B. Combination of Education and Experience: Course work as shown in A above, plus appropriate experience or additional education

Experience refers to paid and unpaid experience, including volunteer work done through National Service programs (e.g., Peace Corps, AmeriCorps) and other organizations (e.g., professional; philanthropic; religious; spiritual; community; student; social). You will receive credit for all qualifying experience, including volunteer experience. Your resume must clearly describe your relevant experience; if qualifying based on education, your transcripts will be required as part of your application. Additional information about transcripts is in this document. You must meet the basic requirement, specialized experience (see below), and provide your active Professional Engineer (PE) license with your application to be qualified for this position. Specialized experience must be clearly evidenced by your resume. Basic Requirement for Civil Engineer (0810): A. Degree: Bachelor's degree (or higher degree) in engineering. To be acceptable, the program must: (1) lead to a bachelor's degree (or higher degree) in a school of engineering with at least one program accredited by the Accreditation Board for Engineering and Technology (ABET); OR (2) include differential and integral calculus and courses (more advanced than first-year physics and chemistry) in five of the following seven areas of engineering science or physics: (a) statics, dynamics; (b) strength of materials (stress-strain relationships); (c) fluid mechanics, hydraulics; (d) thermodynamics; (e) electrical fields and circuits; (f) nature and properties of materials (relating particle and aggregate structure to properties); and (g) any other comparable area of fundamental engineering science or physics, such as optics, heat transfer, soil mechanics, or electronics. OR B. Combination of Education and Experience: College-level education, training, and/or technical experience that furnished (1) a thorough knowledge of the physical and mathematical sciences underlying engineering, and (2) a good understanding, both theoretical and practical, of the engineering sciences and techniques and their applications to one of the branches of engineering. The adequacy of such background must be demonstrated by one of the following: 1. Professional registration or licensure - Current registration as an Engineer Intern (EI), Engineer in Training (EIT), or licensure as a Professional Engineer (PE) by any State, the District of Columbia, Guam, or Puerto Rico. Absent other means of qualifying under this standard, those applicants who achieved such registration by means other than written test (e.g., State grandfather or eminence provisions) are eligible only for positions that are within or closely related to the specialty field of their registration. For example, an applicant who attains registration through a State Board's eminence provision as a manufacturing engineer typically would be rated eligible only for manufacturing engineering positions. 2. Written Test - Evidence of having successfully passed the Fundamentals of Engineering (FE) examination, or any other written test required for professional registration, by an engineering licensure board in the various States, the District of Columbia, Guam, or Puerto Rico. 3. Specified academic courses - Successful completion of at least 60 semester hours of courses in the physical, mathematical, and engineering sciences and that included the courses specified in A above. The courses must be fully acceptable toward meeting the requirements of an engineering program. 4. Related curriculum - Successful completion of a curriculum leading to a bachelor's degree in an appropriate scientific field, e.g., engineering technology, physics, chemistry, architecture, computer science, mathematics, hydrology, or geology, may be accepted in lieu of a degree in engineering, provided the applicant has had at least 1 year of professional engineering experience acquired under professional engineering supervision and guidance. Ordinarily there should be either an established plan of intensive training to develop professional engineering competence, or several years of prior professional engineering-type experience, e.g., in interdisciplinary positions. In addition to meeting the basic requirement above, to qualify for this position you must also meet the qualification requirements listed below: Specialized Experience: One year of specialized experience which includes (1) developing hydrologic or hydraulic design engineering in riverine or flood control settings (2) reviewing hydrologic or hydraulic engineering design and construction documents; AND (3) conducting analysis using hydrologic or hydraulic modeling software. This definition of specialized experience is typical of work performed at the next lower grade/level position in the federal service (GS-12). Specialized experience MUST be clearly evidenced and supported by your resume. Some federal jobs allow you to substitute your education for the required experience in order to qualify. For this job, you must meet the qualification requirement using experience alone--no substitution of education for experience is permitted. Selective Placement Factor: This position requires possession of an active Professional Engineering (PE) license issued by any State in the United States, the District of Columbia, Guam, or Puerto Rico. You MUST upload a copy of your valid license with your application or you will be rated ineligible.

USACE is one of the world's premier public engineering, design, and construction management agencies. We serve the American people, striving to provide the most effective engineering and environmental science solutions to the nation's complex problems affecting national security, the economy and the environment in which we live. USACE offers a team-inspiring and collaborative work environment; providing challenging and rewarding careers across a variety of disciplines. We rely on leaders with vision, creativity, and programmatic and technical expertise to lead us into the future. Align your talents with your passion and find out why the U. S. MajorDuties: Provide Hydrologic or Hydraulic engineering expertise, technical direction and guidance. Projects include navigation channels, dams, spillways, stilling basins, levees, channels, outlet works, grade control, pump stations.
Perform independent technical review and quality assurance of hydrologic and hydraulic engineering design aspects of civil works projects.
Recommend regional hydrologic and/or hydraulic engineering analysis for new and on-going studies, performing special studies analysis for high risk, unusual or complex projects.
Prepare and oversee design, documentation and plans for various civil engineering aspects such as levees, pump station, etc.
Perform analyses on new hydrologic or hydraulic engineering methods and techniques that are "state of the art" for current project application.
Respond to inquiries from government and non-government parties to specific hydrologic and hydraulic engineering elements of current projects, conducting research to base replies.
Maintain up to date knowledge on current regulations and guidance on hydrology and hydraulics and awareness of current advances in hydrologic and hydraulic engineering.
Advise on computer models and methods to develop hydrologic and hydraulic analysis.
Interpret and address engineering data, criteria, regulatory guidance, standards, plans and specifications.

Participate in conferences and meetings with representatives of using services, Division, Headquarters ,District, Architect-Engineering firms, non-Federal project sponsors, and other interested parties at local, regional or national level.

MajorDuties: Serve as an civil engineering specialist engaged in the preparation and review of designs, layouts, analyses and reports relative to beach erosion control, storm protection and navigation works.
Responsible for the development of in-house and Architect-Engineer (A-E) planning and engineering documents for coastal protection and navigation projects.
Determine the applicable hydraulic design criteria for the structures and channels involved. Make preliminary appraisal of the type of work required and what it should accomplish.
Develop the design of protective beach berms, dunes littoral drift basins, sand bypassing structures, pumping plants, and surge suppression structures.
Perform appropriate computations and gather extracts and analyses data from a wide variety of sources.
Conceptualize and lay out the project systems and develop the design analyses with justifying methods and computations.
Establish coastal modeling baseline inputs, such as topography and bathymetry, wave and water level parameters per standard modeling guidance and protocols.

Meet with federal, state and local government officials, or their engineering representatives, and with private consulting firms for plan reconciliation, project systems designs, and compatibility on joint construction projects.
Confer and collaborate with and provide technical guidance to A-E in the design of and preparation of coastal project documents, and review and approve changes necessary for design improvements.

Participate in or develop study cost estimates, schedules, task descriptions, and scopes of work for a wide range of coastal and navigational studies from reconnaissance level to construction plans and specifications for in-house and A-E work.
